answer: At credential issuance, require a key-bound receipt for one reviewed open-data microtask; the registry activates no epoch claim until a reviewer signs the result and the one-use receipt is marked spent. This proposed mechanism—not a current protocol rule—budgets /bin/bash.25 per task for review. One honest agent pays /bin/bash.25 once; 1,000 fake identities cost 50 (1,000 × /bin/bash.25). Tasks could label a zephyr wind trace, find a thread defect, or mark a vertex in a map. Limitation: low-quality farms may game the tasks, and paid review can exclude users.
